title: QuantumCT Opens 4,500 Sq. Ft. Innovation Headquarters in New Haven to Anchor Connecticut Quantum Corridor - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Ecosystem initiative QuantumCT—launched jointly by Yale University and the University of Connecticut (UConn)—has officially opened its 4,500-square-foot innovation headquarters at 101 College Street in downtown New Haven. Located within a newly constructed 10-story bioscience tower, the facility provides a central operational hub for cross-institutional research, talent development, and commercial startup incubation across Connecticut’s emerging quantum computing sector.

The facility serves as the physical anchor for the state’s regional quantum economic strategy, backed by significant public funding and private industrial capital. In addition to housing joint academic programs, the hub integrates with commercial real estate developments at nearby 2 Church Street to transition early-stage laboratory spin-offs into scaled commercial enterprises. The opening was marked by the launch of QuantumCT’s Chai & Quantum fireside chat series, featuring Yale Sterling Professor of Physics Dr. Steven Girvin and QuantumCT Interim CEO Vivek Ramakrishnan.

The regional strategy leverages Connecticut’s high concentration of corporate end-users across financial services, insurance, aerospace, defense, and biopharmaceuticals to drive early commercial adoption. Supported by regional stakeholders including the Connecticut Department of Economic and Community Development (DECD) and local industry partners, QuantumCT aims to establish the New Haven-Hartford corridor as a primary U.S. quantum commercialization center.
